To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
'the procedural semantics of a rule-based system can be modelled by an abstract interpretation of its concrete semantics'.

'The analysis of rule bases is simplified by modelling the procedural semantics, and that the abstract domain can be used for both the analysis of rule base behaviour and the proof of correctness of rule base implementations'.

the abstract interpretation of the procedural semantics of a rule base is useful for the analysis of the rule base's input/output mapping, for the detection of redundancies and for the verification of a rule base against its specification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of rule-based systems in order to improve the reliability and maintainability of expert systems.

the application of abstract interpretation to rule-based systems, in particular, with the use of abstract interpretation to: 1) analyse the behaviour of rule-based systems and to detect redundancies, 2) prove that rule-based systems meet their specification.
the analysis of rule bases which are written in languages which support the procedural semantics of inference engines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the abstract interpretation of a rule base is a powerful and general method for the analysis and validation of rule-based systems.
AbsPS provides a practical and efficient tool for the analysis of rule-based systems.
the abstract interpretation of the procedural semantics of a rule base can be used to analyse the rule base's behaviour, and to prove its correctness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a tool for the analysis of rule-based systems, based on their procedural semantics, which can be applied to rule bases of any complexity.
the abstract description of the input-output mapping is a useful tool for analysing the behaviour of a rule base.
the abstract interpretation approach is an attractive way of analysing rule bases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by modelling the procedural semantics, it is possible to develop a powerful analysis tool for rule-based systems.
, for the analysis of rule-based systems, it is not necessary to model the concrete semantics of the inference engine.
, in order to analyse rule-based systems, we need a method which models the procedural aspects of the language.
